title: Final 2025 regional budget deliberations
subtitle: Also covered: transit fares, Food Bank grant, police and library budgets, homelessness funding, and rejected service cuts.
overview: On final budget day the committee worked through staff's reduction options, service expansions, and the police and library budgets. Staff's running tally, which included the expansions discussed, stood at a 9.79% combined tax increase, well above the original goal of under 8%. Without any expansions it would have been 8.74%.

Most reduction options were defeated, including cuts to GRT routes, adult and children's dental services, discretionary benefits, counselling funding, downtown waste collection and shelter security. The committee recommended delaying the Doon Village reopening to 2026, raising the GRT monthly pass while freezing the affordable transit pass, and charging rent to non-municipal users of the emergency services training centre.

It also recommended trimming the chronic homelessness plan expansion, funding the police and library budgets, raising the Food Bank grant to $1.5 million, and delaying Walker Road. A Vista Hills transit route was deferred to April, and the waste cart staffing expansion was pushed to February pending a staff report. These are recommendations for Council to adopt or change later.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended delaying the reopening of Doon Village to 2026, with the site staying open for rental, for a 2025 reduction of $356,000 {{vote:m15}}.
The committee recommended raising the GRT monthly pass to $104 from the proposed $100 while keeping the affordable transit program pass at its current rate for 2025 {{vote:m22}}.
The committee recommended a 2025 levy impact of $4,685,000 for the plan, after an amendment deferring $2 million tied to a second hybrid shelter {{vote:m53}}.
The committee recommended extending two temporary bylaw officer positions for 2025 only, funded from the tax rate stabilization reserve {{vote:m43}}.
The committee recommended the Waterloo Regional Police Service 2025 operating budget, with a property tax levy of $252,468,301 {{vote:m89}}.
The committee recommended raising the annual Food Bank of Waterloo Region grant to $1.5 million, an additional $756,000, with the cost-of-living clause removed {{vote:m91}}.
The committee recommended updating the fees and charges by-law so children aged 6 and under ride free, with fare changes in July 2025 {{vote:m96}}.
The committee recommended delaying the Walker Road project and cutting the 2025 transportation capital reserve contribution by $465,000 on a one-time basis {{vote:m111}}.

debate: Affordability dominated early debate. Some councillors pointed to overdue property taxes and household strain and suggested deferring the final vote to January. Others said delay would leave residents uncertain and that no new information would emerge.

On reduction options, many councillors opposed cuts to services used by vulnerable people, such as dental programs, counselling and discretionary benefits. Staff repeatedly noted these were options requested by Council, not staff recommendations.

Training centre rent: several councillors said area municipalities helped fund the facility on the understanding that no rent would be charged. The committee narrowed the proposal to Conestoga College and other non-municipal users.

On service expansions, some councillors questioned the growth in staffing and asked for business cases. Staff said expansions had already been cut substantially, and that water, transit and public health demands were rising with population growth.

On the Food Bank grant, supporters cited record demand and the link between food and housing stability. Opponents said it is a provincial and federal responsibility and objected to adding a permanent cost to the levy.
